rto.text: # design basis (Baliga ch.3, parallel plane, silicon):
# BV_PT = Ec*W - (q*N/2eps)*W^2 = ~1407 V -> 17% margin on 1.2 kV
# NPT at same BV would need 119 um of drift at 1.3e14
# tau = 1 us -> La = 42 um vs drift half-width d = 40 um, d/La = 0.94
# a plain voltage sweep cannot step through the vertical avalanche knee
# so ramp in voltage to well below bv then hand off to the load-line
# tracer, which controls on current and can round the turning point
title 1.2kV Si PiN Diode - Reverse Breakdown (curvetrace)

ATLAS>
# gentle off the origin, then open up the depletion sweep in voltage.
# stop short of breakdown - the plain sweep showed only leakage out to
# -1878 v with no avalanche, so ramp to -1500 in voltage and let
# curvetrace carry it the rest of the way, wherever bv actually is
# below mincur it uses voltage steps (step.init grown by nextst.ratio),
# above mincur it switches to the load line and controls on current so
# it can trace through the vertical knee. leakage sits near 1e-13 a and
# noise reaches ~1e-11, so mincur=1e-10 clears both. curr.cont with
# end.val=1e-8 stops once well past the 1e-9 a (0.1 a/cm2) extract point
curvetrace contr.name="anode" step.init=-5.0 nextst.ratio=1.2 mincur=1e-10 end.val=1e-8 curr.cont
